learning_outcomes.text: Has knowledge about the basic fluid properties and the fundamental concepts of the fluid mechanics.
Can derive and apply the fundamental equation of fluid statics and determine the hydrostatic force acting on immersed surfaces.
Can derive and apply the conservation equations of mass, momentum, energy and angular momentum in integral form.
Can analyze incompressible flow in pipes and closed conduits.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION: Definition of fluid, fluid mechanics in engineering, scope of fluid mechanics, methods of analysis, dimensions and units.
FUNDAMENTAL CONCEPTS: Definition of continuum, fluid as a continuum, velocity field, timeline, pathline, streakline and streamline. Stress field. EXPERIMENT I
FUNDAMENTAL CONCEPTS: Viscosity, Newtonian and non-Newtonian fluids, vapor pressure and surface tension, description and classification of fluid motion.
FLUID STATICS: The basic equation of fluid statics, analysis of hydrostatic force on plane submerged surfaces.
FLUID STATICS: Analysis of hydrostatic force on curved submerged surfaces. Buoyancy and stability.
FLUID STATICS: Analysis of fluids in rigid-body motion.
BASIC EQUATIONS FOR A SYSTEM: Conservation of mass, momentum, moment of momentum and energy equations.
BASIC EQUATIONS FOR A SYSTEM: Conservation of mass, momentum, moment of momentum and energy equations. EXPERIMENT II
BASIC EQUATIONS IN INTEGRAL FORM: Derivation of Reynolds transport equation. Derivation and application of conservation of mass and momentum equation.
BASIC EQUATIONS IN INTEGRAL FORM: Derivation and application of moment of momentum and conservation of energy equations for a control volume.
ANALYSIS OF INTERNAL INCOMPRESSIBLE FLOW: Derivation of extended Bernoulli equation. Calculation of major and minor head losses.
ANALYSIS OF INTERNAL INCOMPRESSIBLE FLOW: Flow analysis in serial system of pipes, flow analysis in parallel system of pipes.
ANALYSIS OF INTERNAL INCOMPRESSIBLE FLOW: Analysis of pipe networks, analysis of interconnected reservoir systems.
ANALYSIS OF INTERNAL INCOMPRESSIBLE FLOW: Analysis of pipe networks, analysis of interconnected reservoir systems.
bibliography: Mechanics of Fluids, M. C. Potter and D. C. Wiggert, Prentice Hall.

1) Introduction to Fluid Mechanics, R. W. Fox, P. J. Pritchard and A. T. McDonald, John Wiley & Sons, Inc. 2)Introduction to Fluid Mechanics, D. F. Young, B. R. Munson, T. H. Okiishi and W.W. Huebsch, John Wiley & Sons, Inc.
